newsitem.title: UK: Police to probe bribe claim against UK Labour MP.
newsitem.headline: Police to probe bribe claim against UK Labour MP.

text.p: A new Labour member of parliament on Sunday requested an urgent police investigation of newspaper allegations that he had bribed a rival to lose in Britain's general election two weeks ago.

Millionaire businessman Mohammed Sarwar, who became Britain's first Moslem member of parliament when he won the Glasgow constituency of Govan, denied the claims in The News of the World and said he might sue for libel.

"The allegations about me in today's newspapers are totally false. Therefore, in addition to co-operating with any police investigation, I will be consulting my lawyers tomorrow about taking out a writ for defamation," Sarwar said in a statement.
The statement was issued after Sarwar, who was summoned from Scotland, held talks in London with Nick Brown, Labour's chief whip, or parliamentary business manager.
Brown said he would consider asking the party's National Executive Committee whether to mount an internal inquiry into the allegations.

The News of the World alleged that Sarwar paid 5,000 pounds ($8,000) to an independent Labour candidate, also a Moslem, to get him to ease off campaigning so as not to split both the Labour and Asian vote.

Sarwar said he had asked Scottish Secretary Donald Dewar to request the Procurator Fiscal -- who serves as public prosecutor in Scotland's legal system -- to investigate the claims "as a matter of urgency".
Dewar promised an "immediate and rigorous investigation" and said the allegations were a matter of serious concern.

The claims are the first dark cloud to gather over Tony Blair's government, which has set a cracking pace since it was swept to power on a promise of change from a Conservative administration riddled with suspicions of financial and sexual impropriety after 18 years in power.
Scottish police have already been investigating allegations over late voter registrations in the Govan constituency, which Sarwar won by 2,914 votes.
Sarwar, 46, moved to Scotland from Pakistan at the age of four. He built up a successful cash and carry business and has been involved in the Labour Party for more than 10 years.
